originalTitle: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds
title: Big Helpers Need Helping Hands: Keeping Hospitals Safe in Sudan!
content:
Hello, super kids! Today we have some important news from a country called Sudan. Sudan is a very big country in Africa, just like ours! It has sunny deserts and a huge river called the Nile. But right now, there are some sad things happening there. Some grown-ups are fighting, and it's making things difficult for everyone, especially children.

What is a Hospital?

Do you know what a hospital is? It's a very special building. It's where doctors and nurses work super hard every day. They help people when they are sick or hurt. They give medicine to make you feel better. They even help new baby brothers and sisters be born! Hospitals are truly amazing places. **Did you know?** The very first hospitals were made a very, very long time ago! Even before your great-grandparents were born!

Why Hospitals Are Super Special Places

Imagine if you fell down and scraped your knee really badly. Or if your tummy hurt so much you couldn't eat. A hospital is the place you would go to get help. It's a place where everyone can get care. No matter who they are, hospitals help them. It's a place of healing and hope for everyone. Because hospitals help everyone, they should always be safe. They should be safe for the doctors, the nurses, and especially for the sick children inside.

The Sad News from Sudan

Sadly, in Sudan, some hospitals are getting hurt. People who are fighting, called the RSF fighters, are sometimes going to these hospitals on purpose. They are damaging the buildings. This makes it very hard for doctors and nurses to do their important work. Think about how scary that would be for sick people and little children. **Did you know?** There are over 1.4 billion children living in Africa! That's a lot of kids who need safe places to grow up and play.

Who Are the RSF Fighters?

The RSF fighters are one group of people who are fighting in Sudan. They are soldiers. But they are doing things that hurt people and places that should be safe. It's important to remember that fighting is never good. Especially when it hurts innocent people, like those in a hospital. We wish everyone would choose peace instead of fighting.

What Is a War Crime?

When grown-ups fight, there are still rules. One very important rule is that you must *never* hurt hospitals or the people inside them. Hospitals must always be safe areas. Hurting hospitals on purpose is called a 'war crime.' It's a very, very bad thing to do. It breaks the rules that keep people safe during difficult times. It means someone did something terribly wrong. It's like breaking the biggest rule in the world when it comes to helping others. **Did you know?** A 'crime' is when someone breaks a very important rule or law. A 'war crime' is breaking these special rules during a war or big fight.

People Who Help: Volker Türk and the UN

There are special people in the world who try to make things fair and safe. One of these special people is Mr. Volker Türk. He is a very important helper for the whole world. He works for a big group called the United Nations, or UN for short. The UN helps countries talk to each other. They try to solve problems and keep people safe everywhere. Mr. Türk is saying that hurting hospitals in Sudan might be war crimes. He wants everyone to know that this is not okay. He wants to make sure people are safe and treated fairly. **Did you know?** The United Nations (UN) was started a long time ago. It helps countries work together for peace and safety around the world! Almost every country in the world is a member!

Hopes for Peace and Safety

When we hear sad news like this, it can make us feel a bit worried. But it's important to remember that many people are working hard for peace. They want the fighting to stop in Sudan. They want hospitals to be safe again. They want doctors and nurses to be able to help everyone without fear. We all hope that soon, children in Sudan can go to school and play safely. We hope they can visit hospitals only when they need a little check-up, not because of fighting. **Did you know?** Africa is the second-largest continent in the world! It is full of amazing animals, beautiful places, and many different cultures!

How Can We Help (Even Little Kids!)?

Even though we are far away, we can still help in our hearts. We can hope for peace and safety for the children of Sudan. We can learn about what is happening in the world. And we can always be kind and helpful to the people around us. Because being kind helps make the world a better place for everyone, everywhere. Every little bit of kindness helps.

Conclusion

So, remember, hospitals are very important places. They are for helping, healing, and hope. Hurting them is wrong, and people like Mr. Volker Türk are speaking up about it. We hope for peace and safety for all our friends in Sudan. Let's keep our fingers crossed for a brighter, healthier future for everyone! Thank you for listening, super kids!
summary: Hospitals in Sudan, which are important places for helping sick and hurt people, are being targeted by fighters, and a big world helper named Volker Türk says this might be a very bad wrong thing called a 'war crime.'
whyMatters: This matters because everyone deserves to be safe, especially when they are sick or hurt in a hospital. Hurting hospitals makes it hard for doctors and nurses to help people, which means children and grown-ups might not get the care they need to feel better.

title: Staying Healthy and Happy: A News Report for Super Kids!
content:
Hello, my wonderful friends across Africa! I'm your super kid-friendly news reporter, here to share some important news in a way that's easy for everyone, especially our brilliant Class 2 learners, to understand. Today, we're going to talk about staying healthy and how we can all be super helpers in our communities!

A Special Message from Nigeria

We heard a little story from a country called Nigeria, which is a lovely place, just like where many of you live! There was a lady there who wasn't feeling very well. Doctors, who are like health detectives, found out she had a tiny germ called Ebola. Now, this lady has a husband. He is not sick at all, which is super good news! But to be extra careful, he is staying in a special place by himself for a little while. This is called 'isolation'. It's like taking a little time out to make sure no tiny germs want to play hide-and-seek with him. This helps keep everyone safe and healthy. The grown-ups in charge, called Swiss officials, told us this. They are making sure everything is done carefully to keep people safe. It’s all about being careful and looking after each other.

What is this 'Ebola' Germ?

So, what is this 'Ebola' we're talking about? Well, imagine something super, super tiny, so tiny you cannot see it with your eyes. We call these tiny things 'germs' or 'viruses'. Ebola is one kind of these tiny germs. These tiny germs can sometimes make people feel very sick. It's not like a little sniffle or a small cough; it can make people feel very tired and unwell. But don't worry, it's not a germ that flies around easily in the air when someone sneezes, like some other colds. It mostly spreads when you touch someone who is very, very sick, or touch their blood or other body fluids without being careful. That's why doctors wear special clothes, like superheroes, to protect themselves when they help sick people. Did you know? Germs are super tiny, like invisible little specks! You can't see them, but they are all around us. Some germs are good, but some can make us sick. That's why we learn how to keep them away!

How Can We Stay Super Safe?

The best news is that we can all be super helpers in staying safe from germs, including Ebola and many others! It's actually very simple and fun to do. The most important thing? Washing your hands! Yes, with soap and clean water. Imagine bubbles chasing away all the tiny germs from your hands. Wash them for as long as it takes to sing 'Happy Birthday' twice! Get between your fingers, on your palms, and the back of your hands. Did you know? Washing your hands properly with soap and water can get rid of so many different kinds of germs! It's like having magic super powers for cleanliness! Another way to stay safe is to not touch people who are very sick, especially if you see them bleeding or vomiting. Grown-ups, like doctors and nurses, know how to help these people safely with special protection. Also, if you ever feel unwell, or if your tummy hurts, or you have a fever, tell a grown-up straight away – your mum, dad, teacher, or guardian. They will help you. It's always good to talk about how you feel.

Our Amazing Health Heroes!

We have so many amazing heroes in our communities! Our doctors and nurses are like real-life superheroes. They work so hard to help people who are sick feel better. They are brave and kind. When they help someone with a germ like Ebola, they wear very special suits, masks, and gloves. These special clothes keep them safe from the tiny germs, just like a knight wears armour to be safe in a story! Did you know? Many doctors and nurses in Africa are super heroes, helping people every day! They learn so much to keep us healthy and safe. Let's remember to thank them for their brave work! They are learning more and more every day about how to fight these germs. Scientists, who are like super-smart detectives, are also working hard to find special medicines to make people healthy again.

Let's Be Strong Together!

It's important to remember that Ebola is not everywhere, and many, many people are safe and healthy. When we all follow the simple rules of staying clean and telling grown-ups when we don't feel well, we help stop germs from spreading. Our communities are strong when we look out for each other. Be kind to everyone, even if they are sick, and always listen to your parents and teachers about staying safe and healthy. Did you know? When everyone in a community works together, it makes everyone safer and stronger! We can all be part of the big team that keeps our village or city healthy. So, let's keep washing those hands, playing outside, learning lots, and being happy and healthy kids! We are all part of a big, loving African family, and together, we can keep everyone safe. See you next time, super kids!
summary: A lady in Nigeria had a tiny germ called Ebola, but her husband is safe and staying separate to keep everyone healthy, and we all can help by washing our hands and listening to grown-ups.
whyMatters: This story matters because it helps us learn about tiny germs like Ebola, how to stay safe by washing our hands and telling grown-ups if we feel unwell, and how doctors and nurses are brave heroes helping everyone.

originalTitle: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
title: Helpers Come After a Very Sad Day in a Faraway Land
content:
Hello, hello, my wonderful little friends! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here, bringing you important news from far away. Today, we have a story that makes us feel a little sad, but it also shows us how many good helpers there are in the world. We are going to talk about something that happened in a country called Jordan. Jordan is very, very far from us here in Africa. It's across the big blue ocean!

A Very Sad Day for Many People

Imagine a special building, like a big hall or a church, where grown-ups gather. Sometimes, grown-ups go to a place called a church to pray. Other times, they go for a very special and sad gathering called a funeral. A funeral is a time when families and friends say goodbye to someone they loved very much who has sadly died. It's a time for hugging and sharing memories. Now, in this faraway place called Jordan, many people were at a church for a funeral. They were all there to say goodbye to someone special. But then, something very, very sad and unexpected happened. Some bad grown-ups caused big trouble. This trouble made many, many people feel scared and sad. Because of the trouble, some grown-ups got hurt. And very, very sadly, seven grown-ups died. This made their families and friends feel a huge sadness in their hearts. It was a very, very hard day for them in that part of Jordan.

Many People Needed Help

When the bad trouble happened, it wasn't just a few people who got hurt. A lot of grown-ups got hurt. Can you imagine? Thirty-four grown-ups got hurt and needed help. They needed doctors and nurses to make them feel better and safe again. This was a very, very scary time for all of them. **Did you know?** A church is a special building where people go to pray, sing, and be together. Sometimes, special events like weddings and funerals happen there too. It's usually a peaceful place!

Wonderful Helpers Came Running!

Even though something so sad happened, there is also good news to share. As soon as the trouble started, wonderful, kind helpers came running! Doctors and nurses rushed to the church. Ambulances, those special cars with flashing lights and loud sirens, came very quickly to take the hurt people to the hospital. At the hospital, brave doctors and nurses worked so, so hard. They used their clever hands and kind hearts to help everyone who was hurt. They gave them medicine and comfort to help them feel better. It shows us that even when bad things happen, there are always good people who want to help others. **Did you know?** Doctors and nurses are like real-life superheroes! They study for many years to learn how to fix broken bones, give medicine, and make people healthy again. They help people feel safe and loved when they are sick or hurt.

Police Are Looking for the Bad Guys

After the sad event, the police also came very quickly. Police officers are special grown-ups whose job is to keep everyone safe. They wear uniforms and have special cars to help them do their important work. The police in Jordan are working super hard right now. They are looking for the bad grown-ups who caused all this trouble. They want to find them to make sure they can't hurt anyone else ever again. This search is sometimes called a "manhunt," which just means the police are searching very carefully for specific people. **Did you know?** Police officers help us in many ways! They help us find our way if we get lost, keep traffic safe, and make sure everyone follows the rules to keep our communities happy and safe.

Where Is Jordan?

Let's talk a little more about Jordan. It's a country that is very, very far away from us. If you looked at a big map of the world, you would see Africa, where we live, and then if you went far, far across the sea, you would find Jordan. It's in a place called the Middle East. The place where this sad event happened is called Karak. Karak is like a very big town or a special area within Jordan. Just like how we have different cities and regions in our own countries, Jordan has places like Karak. **Did you know?** The world is a giant, wonderful ball! There are so many different countries with different people, different animals, and different plants all over it. Jordan is just one of many amazing countries!

We Are Safe Here, My Friends!

Now, my little friends, it's very important to remember something. This very sad thing happened far, far away from where we are. It is very rare for such a terrible thing to happen. It does not happen every day, and it does not happen in most places. Grown-ups who take care of you – like your parents, your teachers, and your community leaders – work very, very hard every single day to keep you safe and sound. You are safe, and you are loved. It's okay to feel a little bit sad when you hear news like this, but remember that there are always, always good helpers and kind people in the world. **Did you know?** Your home is a safe space, and your school is a safe space! Grown-ups make rules and plans to make sure you are protected and happy every single day.

Let's Send Our Love and Hope

So, today, let's send our kind thoughts and good wishes to the people in Jordan who are feeling sad. We hope that the grown-ups who got hurt will get better very, very soon. We also hope that the police find the bad grown-ups quickly so that everyone can feel safe again. Let this story remind us to always be kind to each other. A kind word or a helping hand can make a big difference every day. That's all for today's news report, my little friends. Remember to be kind, be brave, and stay safe! See you next time!
summary: In Jordan, a faraway country, a very sad event happened at a church funeral where some grown-ups died and many got hurt, but wonderful helpers like doctors, nurses, and police quickly came to help and keep everyone safe.
whyMatters: This story matters because it shows us that even when very sad and scary things happen, there are always good people who come to help, like doctors and police, and it reminds us to be kind to each other and that grown-ups work hard to keep us safe.
